clue.text: Conflict between evangelist and medium lacking conviction

indicators.note: between says one piece sits in the middle, flanked by the other two

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: A quarrel between a Gospel writer and a spiritualist who lacks real belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm describes half-hearted enthusiasm, someone tepid and without strong commitment to a cause.

clue.text: Passionate desire regarding glory

parts.note: lust is strong passionate craving
re means concerning or regarding, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A lover's burning desire about fame and splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is figurative brilliance or distinction, the shine of renown, so it matches glory.

clue.text: Wake, not half upset about loud commotion

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so the first two of its four letters are dropped

parts.note: the second half of the word wake

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to ruffle someone is to upset or disturb them
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Someone woken up, half of them annoyed by a noisy fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does not wrap the whole word: the loud letter goes inside, just after its first letter. Forte is the musical term for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a fuss or disturbance, an informal word for noisy commotion or disorder.

clue.text: Sequence of days inadequate for hearing

indicators.note: we are told to judge the word by how it is heard spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: weak means feeble or inadequate

explanation.surface: A few days set aside for a court hearing turns out to be too short.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is a run of seven consecutive days, so it is a sequence of days.

clue.text: Run hard, followed by mutated aliens in unusual state

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: something mutated has changed its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the six letters reshuffled
odd means strange or unusual

explanation.surface: Fleeing at speed from mutant extraterrestrials in some strange place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is a US state here, not a condition; the jumbled letters sit inside the word for unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhode Island is the smallest of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Hard to understand old memorial with line missing

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a plaque is a commemorative tablet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An ancient monument's inscription is unreadable because a line has worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque in its figurative use means obscure or unclear, not easily grasped by the mind.

clue.text: Spread support with notice outside entrance

parts.note: a prop holds something up

indicators.note: outside says one piece goes around the other on both sides

parts.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
a gate is an entrance through a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Spreading the word of support by pinning a notice to the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate a plant or idea is to spread or disseminate it widely, so the past tense matches spread.

clue.text: Sound made by duck that's fake

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the call a duck makes
second meaning: a charlatan, especially a bogus doctor

explanation.surface: A duck's call that turns out to be counterfeit, perhaps from a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both the noise of a duck and a sham medical practitioner, used adjectivally for bogus remedies.

clue.text: Eligible to be named

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having the right to something

explanation.surface: Someone qualifies to receive a name or title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having a rightful claim, and also bearing a given title, as a book carries its name.

clue.text: Inspector, very sour, perplexed

indicators.note: being perplexed is being muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy, baffled official checking things over.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor examines land or buildings professionally, a kind of inspector of property and sites.

clue.text: Business with type of curry lacking one element

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so something is removed from the dish

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked in a wok-like pan
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A firm running a curry house, short of one ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a hard bluish metallic chemical element, atomic number 27, used in alloys and pigments.

clue.text: King not in for defeat

parts.note: R is for rex, Latin for king
not in means away or out

explanation.surface: A monarch absent from his palace, leading to his downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat, and to rout an enemy is to beat them decisively.

clue.text: Spoilsport being vacuous in silly tweet

indicators.note: silly means foolish or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
blank means empty of thought or expression

explanation.surface: A killjoy posting an empty-headed, foolish message on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a person who dampens others' fun, an idiom for a killjoy who spoils enjoyment.

clue.text: Film derived from book with unreal end, strangely right

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written for rearranging
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A movie adapted from a novel whose ending is oddly unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Blade Runner was indeed adapted from Philip K Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
explanation.definitionFit: Blade Runner is Ridley Scott's 1982 science-fiction movie starring Harrison Ford, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Vehicle skirting rocky rise, too rough

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the following letters are shaken into a new order
skirting means going round the edge of, so the vehicle surrounds the rest

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach skirting a craggy hill climb, the ride far too bumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous means noisy and rowdy, and of weather or sea it means rough and stormy.

clue.text: Plead for Oasis to reform? It's a fond illusion

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rearranged into new shape

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan begging the Britpop band Oasis to get back together, a hopeless dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis were a famous British rock band who split in 2009; the question mark nods to fans' hopes of a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool's paradise is an idiom for a state of happiness built on false hopes or self-deception.

clue.text: Broadcast after nice connection between systems

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A programme aired following something pleasant, linking two networks.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is the point where two computer systems or components meet and exchange data.

clue.text: New hotel in prosperous period that is providing conviviality

indicators.note: in says the first pieces go inside the next one

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic growth
ie abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
N is the abbreviation for new
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newly opened hotel in boom times offering a warm, friendly atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and good nature, the genial warmth of convivial company.

clue.text: Condition people to be taken in by obvious exaggeration

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: overt means open and plainly visible
a state is a condition someone is in
men as people in general

explanation.surface: Training people to fall for blatant hyperbole.
explanation.definitionFit: An overstatement says more than the facts warrant, which is exactly what exaggeration does.

clue.text: Teacher vital for stupid person

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
key means crucial or vital

explanation.surface: A tutor's role is essential when dealing with a dim pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow or tutor at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey is a colloquial insult for a fool or dolt, from the animal's reputation for dimness.

clue.text: Dreadful distorted drone in group of singers without leader

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another
something distorted is twisted out of shape, so the letters change order
having no leader means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: a chorus is a body of singers
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful warped drone from a choir that has lost its conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a conductor, but it means only the first letter of the group's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrendous and dreadful are synonyms, both meaning extremely unpleasant or shockingly bad.

clue.text: Unyielding soldier breaking free

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A stubborn soldier escaping from captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and inflexible, refusing to bend, which is what unyielding means.

clue.text: Hesitation? Leave for that reason

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Pausing over whether to depart, and asking why.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to introduce a logical consequence.

clue.text: Potato up in cupboard upstairs

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: A potato stored in a cupboard on the top floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato, common in everyday British and Irish speech.

clue.text: Larval form wise men mostly understood

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity story
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: The three kings largely grasping something about an insect's early stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the soft legless larva of a fly, the grub stage before it pupates.

clue.text: Trick involving snake put back in bag

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a knack is a clever trick or technique

indicators.note: put back means returned the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick where a snake is returned to the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, much like a rucksack or backpack.

clue.text: Part of rebel destined to be greatest in age

indicators.note: part of says the letters are a portion of the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rebel fated to become the oldest of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldest means the oldest, especially of siblings, the superlative of elder.

clue.text: Tramp not having time consumed by boring toil

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed inside it

parts.note: dry means dull or boring

indicators.note: not having means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to tramp or trudge is to walk heavily
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tramp with no time to spare, stuck in monotonous labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring toil' reads as one phrase, but boring is the wordplay and toil alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial and tedious work, which is a form of toil.
